correctness.rationale: For all integers \(m,n\ge3\) the metric on \(K_m\square P_n\) is \(\mathbf1_{a\ne b}+|t-u|\). A vertex is between two others iff it is between their path coordinates and its clique label equals an endpoint label. This proves exhaustively that each gp set uses distinct clique labels, except for one repeated label whose two occurrences bracket every other distinct label. The two disjoint families count to Psi. Their inclusion-maximal subfamilies comprise adjacent repeated pairs, fully occupied repeated-label interiors, and all-label-once assignments excluding two explicitly counted extendibility events; inclusion-exclusion gives M. The derived three facet sizes are nonempty. An independent BFS graph-distance and exhaustive-subset verifier passed 491210 subsets across 29 instances, with direct maximal-set census for seven main-domain products. Those finite checks corroborate but do not substitute for the general proof.

originality.rationale: Both closed enumerators and the exact three-class maximal-set classification are absent from the verified statements of the most pertinent primary papers and published mathematical record results compared. The scalar equality \(\operatorname{gp}(K_m\square P_n)=m+1\) and the lower value two are not presented as novel; the simultaneous full size and facet polynomials are the claim. Closest original proofs contain partial structural ideas but neither supply the all-cardinality enumerator nor an implication that directly determines the facet coefficients. The residual risk of unindexed equivalents is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper may contain the equivalent two-shape classification and direct counting formulas under other terminology.
Tian–Xu Lemma 3.1 shares a necessary part of the repetition obstruction, so historical priority for parts of the structural lemma is limited.
The online-accessible manuscript sections and search index do not guarantee exhaustive review of every related graph-enumeration article.

value.rationale: Cartesian products of a clique and a path form a natural infinite graph family already examined for extremal geodesic general position. The exact all-size generating polynomial and every inclusion-maximal facet coefficient are independently motivated counting invariants beyond known scalar gp and lower gp numbers. Their simultaneous closed descriptions reveal nonpurity with exactly three facet sizes \(2,m,m+1\), and an unbounded separation between the smallest and largest maximal configurations. This provides complete structural enumeration, not a textbook restatement of an extremal value.
